title: An algorithmic approach for computing fundamental domains of crystallographic groups
summary: A crystallographic group is a discrete subgroup of the Euclidean group $\operatorname{E}(n)$ that has a compact fundamental domain. Since such a crystallographic group $Γ$ is infinite, computing fundamental domains of $Γ$ is algorithmically challenging. We address this difficulty by targeting the computation of Dirichlet cells that can form fundamental domains of $Γ$. We show that the half-spaces defining such a Dirichlet cell can be derived from elements of $Γ$ acting on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that can be expressed as words of bounded length in a suitable generating set.
